full_judgment: 13. Mr. Probir Neogi, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of respondent No.1 argued that the petitioners (pre-emptor) are no more a co-sharer in the suit khatian inasmuch as pursuant to their purchase, they got their name mutated in respect of suit land vide aforementioned mutation case and thereby they ceased to be co-sharer in respect of suit land since with the separation of holding from the joint holding and other co-sharer also being ceased to be co-sharer. On the other hand, A.M. Amin Uddin, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the petitioners (preemptor) denied the aforesaid argument and counter argued that it is to be as took into as to whether the notice of separation of holding was proceeding having been served on the co-sharer and mutation being effected behind their back and knowledge, there is no valid splitting up of jama and as such, the co-sharers have not lost their right of pre-emption under section 24 of Non Agricultural Tenancy Act. He further argued that the mutated khatian does not mean that there is the division of holding and by mutation khatian co-sharership does not extinguish the co-sharership and that in a proceeding under section 24 of Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, the petitioners ought to be co-sharer of the land transferred, not in the jama. He also argued that the ingredients of pre-emption under of section 24 of the Non-Agriculture Tenancy Act and those of section 96 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act are different. The expression "holding" in section 96 is not to be found in section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, He finally argued that the sub-division of holding without demarcation on the ground and not shown on the cadastral survey map is not a valid subdivision and the pre-emptee-opposite party failed to prove that after splitting jama, the land was demarcated on the ground by tri-angular pillars and that land was shown on the cadastral survey map.
